packs.title: Lexington beyond the centre
packs.promise: Horses, museum questions and the shapes of a living landscape.

q.s: Build a small timeline from the open museum galleries.
st: Check in for the Horse Park and use only open International Museum of the Horse galleries. Riding, live shows and private barns are outside this mission.
Find three displayed accounts of people using or living with horses. Choose distinct roles rather than three trophies for the same event.
For each, note the displayed object or image, a time or period stated by its label, and the role it explains. Choose another example if the label is unclear.
Order the three records by their stated dates, or explain where a period is too broad to order. Add one connection between a role and life today.

q.s: Notice one stretch of the paved Legacy Trail twice.
st: Start on the open pedestrian side of the Legacy Trail near Coldstream Park. Set a comfortable turnaround before you move.
On the outward stretch, note a fixed path-side feature and a change in the surroundings. Keep your attention on cyclists and the path, not the screen.
Return along the same open path, recognizing the fixed feature from the opposite direction. Shortening the walk still counts.
Record the start, your actual turnaround and what looked different on the return.

q.s: Give a quiet garden setting three undistracted minutes.
st: Choose a permitted path spot with a view of tree canopy and enough room for other visitors to pass. Move elsewhere if a service or family visit is nearby.
Put the phone away for three quiet minutes. Notice light or shadow changing within the canopy; a still or overcast scene is a valid observation.
After the pause, write one present-moment detail and one question about how a place is cared for over time.
Leave the setting as you found it and continue quietly toward the exit before closing.

packs.title: Lexington between Main and Gratz
packs.promise: Historic rooms, street fronts and small acts of making.

q.s: Follow two artefacts beyond their first impression.
st: Check in for the admitted self-guided museum. Choose two objects whose displayed interpretation connects them to a person or household activity.
For each object, write its visible material/form and one label-supported connection. Do not assume every furnishing belonged to Mary Todd Lincoln.
Find one detail that complicates your first impression of life in the house. Use the exhibit or ask staff; mark anything not confirmed as a question.
Make a two-object note card that separates what you saw, what the museum states and what you still wonder.

q.s: Follow a short path above a buried creek.
st: Begin on the open pedestrian trail near South Broadway and choose a comfortable return point before South Upper Street.
As you move, look for one paving detail and one planted edge. Stop clear of other users to save the observations.
Read the City’s linked explanation of the culverted creek; distinguish the historical water route from water you actually see.
Return on the same open path and write how the two surface details make room for movement. A shorter section counts.

q.s: Make room for the worker behind a civic building.
st: Read the short source note: the park’s namesake Henry A. Tandy co-founded Tandy & Byrd, which performed the historic courthouse’s original brickwork.
From an open park spot, choose a visible masonry detail on the adjoining building. Do not claim a particular brick was personally laid by Tandy.
Spend two quiet minutes noticing repetition in the work: spacing, rows, corners or an edge.
Write the detail, the namesake’s sourced connection and one question about the labour needed to build it.
